title: "Synthetic Executable Companion to \u201cExploring Large Document Repositories with RDF Technology: The DOPE Project\u201d"
abstract: "This dataset and documentation package present a synthetic executable companion to the paper \u201cExploring Large Document Repositories with RDF Technology: The DOPE Project.\u201d Generated with the DBbun pipeline, the companion translates key ideas from the source paper into an inspectable computational artifact, including thesaurus-based indexing with EMTREE, RDF-based querying across heterogeneous repositories, co-occurring keyword analysis, hierarchy-aware query expansion, and visualization-oriented exploration of large biomedical document collections. The original paper describes a system that integrates major sources such as Medline and ScienceDirect through a semantic layer designed to support richer discovery and navigation.The generated companion includes a simulator, documented parameters, six simulation scenarios, structured CSV outputs, and multiple figures intended to make the paper\u2019s mechanisms more reusable for experimentation, teaching, and demonstration. According to the documentation, the package contains 22 parameters, of which 13 were extracted from the paper and 9 were assumed, and it covers scenarios such as aspirin-query retrieval, query-expansion depth sweeps, multi-keyword overlap complexity, and user-study-inspired feedback summaries.This resource is intended as a reproducibility-oriented, synthetic companion artifact rather than a reconstruction of the original authors\u2019 validated results. The simulator outputs, datasets, and figures are computationally inspired by the source document and are provided to illustrate the phenomena described in the paper, not to reproduce the original experimental data. Users should therefore treat this package as a supplementary executable interpretation of the paper."

title: Cooperative Task Allocation and Path Optimization of UAV Swarm Based on Genetic-Particle Swarm Hybrid Algorithm
abstract: To overcome traditional algorithms’ limitations (slow convergence, susceptibility to local optima), this study proposes a hybrid genetic-particle swarm algorithm (GPSHA). Integrating GA's global exploration with PSO's rapid convergence via adaptive parameters, GPSHA first establishes a multi-objective model incorporating flight range, time, obstacle avoidance, and task uniqueness constraints. Enhanced by PSO's position-speed update and adaptive crossover-mutation, the hybrid algorithm combines global and local optimization. Simulations show ≥15% faster convergence and 12% lower objective cost, effectively meeting drone swarm collaborative operation requirements.

title: Semantic Network Embedding with Gaussian Distributions
abstract: Knowledge graph embedding aims to represent human knowledge in a machine-interpretable form, enabling downstream language models to better incorporate structured information. Semantic network, as a special form of knowledge graph, organizes abstract conceptual knowledge in a hierarchical structure. Existing knowledge graph embedding methods struggle to preserve the inheritance property inherent in semantic networks. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a novel semantic network embedding framework, SN2E. We interpret abstract concepts as Gaussian distributions in a continuous space, using their mean vectors and covariance matrices as embeddings. Furthermore, we formally implement two fundamental semantic operators—intersection and subsumption. Based on this formulation, we develop an iterative algorithm to efficiently construct and train semantic network embeddings. We build two standardized semantic network datasets and conduct comparative experiments against several state-of-the-art knowledge graph embedding methods on classification tasks. The results demonstrate substantial improvements over existing approaches, and visualization analyses further confirm the rationality of our learned embeddings.

title: Drone Delivery Route Planning for the Low-Altitude Economy: An Improved Gray Wolf Optimization Algorithm Based on Niche Technology
abstract: With the rapid development of the low-altitude economy, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly used in logistics and e-commerce delivery services. Efficient route planning is a key factor affecting the safety, energy consumption, and operational efficiency of UAV delivery systems. However, traditional path planning algorithms often face challenges such as premature convergence and insufficient adaptability in complex low-altitude environments. To address these issues, this paper proposes an improved grey wolf optimization algorithm based on niche technology (NGWO) for UAV delivery route planning. The proposed method integrates a niche-sharing mechanism into the grey wolf optimization framework to enhance population diversity and avoid local optima. Meanwhile, a multi-objective route planning model is constructed by considering flight distance, energy consumption, obstacle avoidance, and delivery efficiency within the low-altitude logistics network. Simulation experiments conducted in a three-dimensional urban environment demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms and Genetic algorithms (GA) traditional GWO in terms of path optimality, convergence speed, and solution stability. The results indicate that the improved algorithm can effectively support UAV logistics operations and provide a reliable optimization framework for the development of the low-altitude economy.

title: Pattern-Aware Graph Neural Networks for Handling Missing Data
abstract: Missing data is ubiquitous in real-world datasets. Traditional methods either discard incomplete samples or apply imputation techniques that ignore potentially informative missingness patterns, implicitly assuming that missingness occurs randomly. However, missingness patterns might provide additional information. We propose pattern-aware graph neural networks that explicitly encode which features are missing alongside observed values. We used four encoding strategies-learned embeddings, frozen random embeddings, statistical features, and hierarchical representations-across seven UCI datasets with naturally occurring missingness. Our Pattern-aware methods achieve substantial improvements over baselines, with an average improvement of $17 \%$ in balanced accuracy and $22 \%$ in F1-macro across all datasets. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/TranMinett/pattern_aware_GRAPE.

title: Detecting Neurovascular Instability from Multimodal Physiological Signals Using Wearable-Compatible Edge AI: A Responsible Computational Framework
abstract: We propose Melaguard, a multimodal ML framework (Transformer-lite, 1.2M parameters, 4-head self-attention) for detecting neurovascular instability (NVI) from wearable-compatible physiological signals prior to structural stroke pathology. The model fuses heart rate variability (HRV), peripheral perfusion index, SpO2, and bilateral phase coherence into a composite NVI Score, designed for edge inference (WCET <=4 ms on Cortex-M4). NVI - the pre-structural dysregulation of cerebrovascular autoregulation preceding overt stroke - remains undetectable by existing single-modality wearables. With 12.2 million incident strokes annually, continuous multimodal physiological monitoring offers a practical path to community-scale screening. Three-stage independent validation: (1) synthetic benchmark (n=10,000), AUC=0.88 [0.83-0.92]; (2) clinical cohort PhysioNet CVES (n=172; 84 stroke, 88 control) - Transformer-lite achieves AUC=0.755 [0.630-0.778], outperforming LSTM (0.643), Random Forest (0.665), SVM (0.472); HRV-SDNN discriminates stroke (p=0.011); (3) PPG pipeline PhysioNet BIDMC (n=53) -- pulse rate r=0.748 and HRV surrogate r=0.690 vs. ECG ground truth. Cross-modality validation on PPG-BP (n=219) confirms PPG morphology classifies cerebrovascular disease at AUC=0.923 [0.869-0.968]. Multimodal fusion consistently outperforms single-modality baselines. Code: https://github.com/ClevixLab/Melaguard

title: The Semantic Binding Engine
abstract: The Semantic Binding Engine: Solving the Ontology Translation GapModern projects generate vast amounts of heterogeneous data—RFID pings, timesheet entries, BIM elements, sensor telemetry, drone imagery, and administrative records. Yet none of these systems share a common ontology. They describe the same real‑world event using incompatible languages, leaving critical relationships invisible and forcing humans to manually reconcile data that should already be unified.This gap is the Missing Ontology Translation Engine: the absence of a mechanism capable of understanding that multiple signals, across multiple systems, all refer to the same underlying task, activity, or physical state.The Semantic Binding Engine provides this missing layer.It is an AI‑driven semantic translator that automatically binds unstructured physical telemetry to structured administrative representations. Using spatial‑temporal proximity, behavioural patterns, and Large Language Models (LLMs), the engine identifies when disparate signals—such as an RFID location ping, a timesheet row, and a 3D BIM polygon—represent the same real‑world action. These signals are merged into a single Unified Node Identity, eliminating the need for manual data entry or cross‑system reconciliation.By resolving semantic fragmentation, the engine enables REM to maintain a coherent, continuously updated relational model of the project or asset. This ensures that design truth, administrative truth, and physical truth remain aligned, and that conflicts or anomalies can be detected and resolved at the relational level rather than through isolated system checks.The Semantic Binding Engine forms a foundational component of REM’s cognitive architecture, enabling automated interpretation, conflict detection, and system‑level coherence across complex, multi‑modal environments.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Modern Industries: Applications, Challenges, and Future Trends
abstract: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Modern Industries: Applications, Challenges, and Future Trends Parth Aland Saint Thomas English Medium School, Solapur, India Dr. Rajivkumar Mente Dept. of Computer Applications, School of Computational Sciences, Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Holkar Solapur University, Solapur, India Dr. Preeti Deshmukh Dept. of Computer Science Engineering, V.V.P. Institute of Engineering & Technology, Solapur, India Dr. Bapu Chendge Dept. of Computer Applications, Central University of Karnataka, Kalburgi, India Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a transformative force in modern industries by enabling intelligent automation, data-driven decision-making, and adaptive operational systems. Advances in machine learning, deep learning, analytics, and Industry 4.0 have accelerated AI adoption across sectors. This paper reviews AI’s evolution, core techniques, applications, benefits, challenges, and future directions in industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, finance, logistics, energy, and retail. It examines how AI improves operational efficiency, reduces costs, enhances product quality, and supports workforce augmentation. At the same time, it highlights major challenges, including data quality, cybersecurity risks, ethical and legal concerns, lack of explain ability, high implementation costs, and workforce skill gaps. The study also discusses emerging trends such as explainable AI, autonomous industrial systems, Industry 5.0 integration, and sustainable green AI. By identifying research gaps and future opportunities, the paper supports responsible, scalable, and sustainable AI adoption for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Industry 4.0, Industrial Automation, Machine Learning, Smart Manufacturing, Industry 5.0

title: pkCNN:A scalable Zero-Knowledge proof for Convolutional Neural Network based on Plonk
abstract: Directly applying compute-intensive tasks in CNN models to general-purpose zero-knowledge proof systems is insufficient to meet practical requirements, as the computational complexity of proof generation and the scale of arithmetic circuits are directly correlated with the amount of computation. Therefore, improving the efficiency of circuit generation is a critical issue that urgently needs to be addressed. This paper proposes pkCNN, which splits the computations in CNN models into two parts for processing. It optimizes the verification of matrix multiplication, a common operation in linear computations, reducing its complexity to O(N). It also converts complex non-linear operations into constraints applicable to the Plonk system. Additionally, the Cached Quotients technique is introduced and enhanced with zero-knowledge properties, which is applied to the Lookup operations derived from the conversion of non-linear operations. The overall running time of pkCNN is approximately 1.5× faster than Baseline, while the SRS size is significantly reduced.

title: Seeing What Few-Shot Learners See: Contrastive Cross-Class Attribution for Explainability
abstract: Few-shot learning (FSL) enables deep learning models to generalize to unseen categories with minimal labeled data, making it crucial for data-constrained domains such as healthcare. However, existing FSL models often lack explainability, obscuring the reasoning behind their predictions and limiting trust in their deployment. In this work, we introduce contrastive cross-class attribution (C3A) to enhance explainability in FSL. Specifically, we present C3A for explaining query predictions and its variant (C3A-E) for episodic learning. Unlike prior explainability methods designed for specific architectures, our approach is classifier-agnostic, leveraging the backbone network to ensure broad applicability across diverse FSL paradigms. In addition, we propose contrastive local descriptors that integrate naive-Bayes nearest-neighbor (NBNN) and Fisher score-based attribution to preserve fine-grained details and enhance interclass discrimination. Finally, we comprehensively evaluate our methods across four FSL benchmarks, demonstrating consistent improvements over state-of-the-art approaches, with absolute gains of 19.72% in insertion-area-under-curve (iAUC) and 25.88% in deletion-area-above-curve (dAAC). Our posthoc design ensures seamless integration with various architectures, including Conv64F, ResNet12, ResNet18, and ViT. The experimental results confirm that C3A and its variant (C3A-E) provide more stable and interpretable explanations compared to existing FSL explainability methods, offering deeper insights into the episodic learning process. We have made our code publicly available at https://github.com/MountainChenCad/C3A.

title: A TD3 Approach Based on Two-Sided Evolutionary Fusion for Robotic Arm Path Planning
abstract: A Two Side Evolutionary Fusion-Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TEA-TD3) method is proposed focused on low planning efficiency along with long and tortuous paths for robotic arm path planning. Firstly, TEA-TD3 utilizes the Improved Cross-Entropy Method (ICEM) to alternately optimize the actor network and the critic network of TD3, thereby obtaining a better critic policy and improving the overall convergence speed. Secondly, hybrid distribution evolutionary perturbation mechanism and elite individual recycling mechanism are proposed. These mechanisms balance the scope of initialization perturbations for the actor network population and reintroduce the best critic network individual from the previous generation into the current population, thereby enhancing the overall explorative capability and stability of the method. Finally, the robotic arm conducts path planning experiments in the Robot Operating System (ROS)-Gazebo simulator. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the ICEM-TD3 and TD3 methods in terms of success rate, average path length, average distance to the target, and average steps to completion.

The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the ICEM-TD3 and TD3 methods in terms of success rate, average path length, average distance to the target, and average steps to completion.
